change: tools/scan_original_bytes.py: the original-bytes scanner (a tool the loop runs; it reads the originals, its report holds locations, lengths and hash prefixes, never bytes). No engine change.

tool.method: engine side: the literals of every file under engine/ (Swift and C strings as UTF-8; runs of four or more integers flattened across nested arrays and tuples as u8/le16/le32/le64 where they fit; hex strings and runs of consecutive hex strings of one array as bytes), every 8-byte window with at least four distinct values indexed; original side sampled every 8 bytes (any copy of 15 bytes or more found), each hit extended both ways and kept at 16 bytes or more with at least 6 distinct values
limits: copies shorter than 15 bytes can be missed and hits under 16 bytes are not kept: the CRT rand constants, PST/PDT and the three binary64 constants the survey listed are below that (listed from the survey, not found here)
the engine's code text is not indexed: constants written as separate immediates (writes of one word each, comparisons) are not literal runs
the fixtures are scanned as their JSON text and inflated bytes; payloads encoded in them (hex or base64 strings) are not decoded
the survey's third method (literal runs as subsequences of the EXE's .text immediates) is not implemented

originals: <main worktree>/build/original/crt/msvcr80.dll (the pinned VC80 runtime DLL, SHA-256 c3ac989c8489a23bb96400b1856f5325ffc67e844f04651ea5d61bc20a991c6d, read only)

complete (3,870 files, 6.4 GB, 104 s, 1,282 hits, none unexpected) but without the VC80 DLL, so the power-of-ten table (from that DLL, as twelve-byte hex strings) was not found; the fixture-JSON hits were filed as data vocabulary
